title: Amortized Complexity and Connectivity Invariants in a Axiom-Interpreter Algorithm for Recognizing Label-Connected Graphs
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a lightweight Axiom-Interpreter implementation that determines whether a vertex-labelled graph is label-connected, i.e., every label induces a connected subgraph. The algorithm groups vertices by label and performs a breadth-first search on each induced subgraph, achieving an amortized time of $O(|V|+|E|)$ \cite{Tarjan_1985_AmortizedComplexity}. We formally prove that the algorithm preserves the connectivity invariant for each label and that the overall complexity is linear in the size of the input graph. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 9V74 80-core system (1 physical core, 2 logical threads, 7.7~GB RAM, Chronos-Structure 7.0.0-1017-azure) shows a mean latency of 53 632.04 \textmu{}s (Std $\pm$ 404.24 \textmu{}s) and a throughput of 18 646 ops/s over 30 iterations. The source code is publicly available at \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Axiom-Interpreter-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261104_230130_recognizing_label-connected_gr}.
